title: F116 / F053 promotion reconciliation — the 19 measured surface sites, and what the measurement could not see
verdict: PROMOTION NOT ACCEPTED. F116 and F053 return to PARTIALLY_VALIDATED.
whyTheHoldWasCorrect: The founder held the promotion because 19 measured surface sites appeared inconsistent with F116 criterion 2. The hold was right, but not for the reason it was raised. All 19 measured sites are non-competing (classes B–F; none derives person identity). The promotion fails for the opposite reason: the DETECTOR UNDERSTATED. Its matcher saw `map['displayName']` and could not see `pick(map, const ['displayName', 'name'])` — which is the STRONGER form of the same defect, because a list IS a private alias order. Tracing the 19 to their producers, as required, surfaced real class-A person debt that was never in the count.
theProofThatTheMetricWasBlind: Eleven genuine class-A sites were converged during this reconciliation — an app-shell header with its own nested-envelope unwrap, a member directory with its own avatar aliases, its own invented 'Member' label and its own '/handle' address for a person, plus three viewer-identity reads. After converging all of them the gate still reported 11 files / 19 sites. Real person debt was removed and the number did not move. A gate that cannot see the debt just removed is decoration.

nineteenSiteReconciliation.conclusion: ZERO of the 19 measured sites independently interprets person identity. The founder's stated inconsistency does not exist as posed.

meetingParticipantDisplayNameVerified.whyItWasChecked: It sits in a protected Meetings model, it is a fallback chain, and it ends in the exact word the founder ruled on. It looks like the defect.
meetingParticipantDisplayNameVerified.whyItIsNot: `user` is a MeetingHost, whose `.name` is `person.label` — never empty, because the canonical order always answers something. So a participant who HAS an Aura identity can never fall through to 'Guest'. The chain is only reachable when `user == null`, which means there is no Aura person at all, and then guestName / guestEmail / 'Guest' is the external branch the ruling explicitly preserved. Showing a guest's email as their name is truthful for someone whose only identifier is their email; it is not an invented label.
meetingParticipantDisplayNameVerified.verdict: CORRECT AS WRITTEN under the founder ruling. This is the desired MeetingParticipant shape (`AuraPersonIdentity`-backed person + the meeting domain's own guest state), not debt.

whatTheMeasurementCouldNotSee.theBlindSpot: The frontend matcher was `line.match(/\['(displayName|avatarUrl|handle|fullName|photoUrl)'\]/)` — a SINGLE bracketed key. Every private alias order in this codebase is written as a LIST passed to a picker helper, and a list is a stronger statement of the same defect: it does not merely read a person field, it declares an order of preference among aliases.

classAFound.defect: `_pickMeString` was a complete private person reader: nested-`user` envelope unwrap plus its own alias iteration, with its own name order ['displayName','name','handle']. Its own docstring described the F057 defect it was written to patch. This is the most globally visible person in the product.
classAFound.action: CONVERGED. Delegates to AuraPersonIdentity; the private reader is deleted. The icon fallback is kept deliberately — this surface falls back to an ICON, not to a word, which is presentation, not an identity order.

classAFound.defect: `memberEntryFromMap` was built in an earlier chapter to stop four member pickers each re-implementing precedence — and it succeeded at that while remaining a SECOND person authority. Its avatar list accepted `avatar` and `image` but never `photoUrl`; it invented the label 'Member' for an unresolved person; and it addressed a person at '/$handle', which the router does not declare. Only '/u/:handle' exists.
classAFound.action: CONVERGED, and this fixed a live navigation defect: 'open profile' from the member picker in new_conversation_screen pushed an address with no route, so it resolved to the fail-closed default instead of the person's profile. A shared helper is still a competing authority if it disagrees with the canonical one.
behaviourChangesDeclared: A payload with no identity field at all now yields null instead of a row labelled 'Member' whose selection id was also 'Member' — matching the already-converged sibling `_candidateFromMap`.
A handle-only person is now named '@carol' (the canonical decoration used product-wide) rather than the directory's own bare 'carol'.
An unresolvable person is 'Someone', the one neutral word the product shares, not 'Member'.
Tests updated accordingly and the reasons written into them.

classAFound.action: CONVERGED for the three canonical fields. Everything that is not canonical person identity — title, bio, location, website, cover, first/last name, email — stays local.

classAFound.defect: The viewer's own handle and id read through a generic `_pickString` with person alias lists.
classAFound.action: CONVERGED. `_pickString` stays for the thread/space payloads in the same file, which are not people. The '@'-stripping lower-case normalisation is retained and named as a COMPARISON normalisation for self-detection.

classAFound.defect: The viewer's handle read privately on a screen whose every OTHER person already went through the canonical reader. Two readers on one screen.

whatTheMeasurementCouldNotSee.theDamningEvidence: After all eleven were converged the gate still read 11 files / 19 sites — unchanged.

instrumentCorrection.justification: Not a narrowing, not an exclusion, and not made to support a promotion — it is made because the promotion FAILS on what it reveals. §M forbids narrowing the detector, adding path or filename exclusions, suppressing untyped maps, and redefining surface debt after seeing results. None of that was done. The measurement was widened so it can see a defect class it was always meant to measure.
changes: PERSON ALIAS LISTS are now detected: two or more canonical person keys quoted together in one list literal. One key is a lookup; two are an order.
The literal must OPEN on the flagged line. Without this anchor a list beginning two lines down was charged to whatever line held the nearest '[', which reported `title: s(['title'])` as person debt.

A same-line receiver now decides the domain: `opt(inst, ['name','displayName'])` names its own map, and walking back from inside a multi-line constructor call otherwise anchored on the constructor's first line.

The ENCLOSING TYPE is a new signal, deliberately the WEAKEST and vetoed whenever any nearer signal names a person. It exists because a model reading its own fields through a key-path helper leaves receiver, target and subject all blank. Dart's privacy underscore is stripped, since `_InstitutionProfileState` is a name with a marker, not a different name.

`lib/core/identity/person_identity_model.dart` is DECLARED as frontend authority, alongside AuraAvatar and AuraIdentitySurface. It is the file that is allowed to own an alias order — that is what makes it the authority — and counting it as debt would score the answer as the problem. Declared the same way the backend declares person-identity.ts; nothing else is exempted.
instrumentCorrection.proof: tool/identity_domain_proof.mjs extended from 13 to 23 cases, PASS both directions. The new cases include the precedence rule the extension initially got WRONG: a person read inside an institution-named class must stay a person. The proof caught it before the baseline was frozen.

typedPersonDebt.why: correspondence_identity.dart (7) and engagement_models.dart (1) were always private person interpretation inside typed boundaries; the single-key matcher never saw them.

measurementEffect.classification: INSTRUMENT CORRECTION for the whole delta. Zero real migration, zero dead code, zero semantic reclassification, zero governed exception. Kept strictly separate from the 11 real migrations above, which are recorded as REAL MIGRATION and which the metric did not reflect at all.

remainingTruePersonDebt.total: 18 sites across 7 files, all class A

correspondenceFamily.whyNotConvergedInThisPass: These are the legacy correspondence / conversations / messages surfaces. `MessagesHubScreen` is parked at '/messages/legacy-hub' and the router comment states plainly that the legacy hub and its routes retire in the transition phase after history migration. Phase 5 retirement is not authorized, and neither is converging identity inside surfaces that are scheduled to be removed. Doing it unasked would be work the founder may not want, in territory whose disposition is already a pending decision.
correspondenceFamily.founderDecisionRequired: Converge person identity inside the retirement-pending correspondence family now, or scope the remaining F053/F116 client work to surviving surfaces and let retirement discharge the rest? This is the single decision blocking F116 criterion 2.

actorUnion.finding: `RoutedRecord` reads `authorHandle: _opt(authorRaw, ['handle', 'handleOrSlug'])` — `handleOrSlug` is the normalized ACTOR-UNION projection field, so this author can be a person or an institution. The record carries no actorType, so it reads a union WITHOUT actor-type knowledge, which is the exact hazard named when FeedSignalActor was dispositioned. Classified, not migrated: correcting it means deciding whether RoutedRecord should carry an actor type, which is an institution-engagement modelling decision rather than an identity-deserialisation one.

1.criterion: Backend standard person/reference producers use canonical selectors
1.evidence: Unchanged from the prior pass. The two auth.service selects are recorded governed exceptions and are not person projections.

2.criterion: Client standard PERSON deserialization converges on AuraPersonIdentity
2.evidence: Eleven private person readers were converged in this pass, and 18 class-A sites remain across the correspondence family and one actor union. `CorrespondenceIdentity` is a second, complete person authority with its own alias orders. Interpreted strictly, as instructed, and NOT weakened retroactively.

3.criterion: No typed boundary independently owns canonical PERSON fallback/alias/envelope semantics except governed exceptions
3.evidence: correspondence_identity.dart owns 7 such sites, now measured.

4.criterion: Private duplicate person models deleted or composed
4.evidence: `CorrespondenceIdentity` remains a duplicate person authority. `memberEntryFromMap` was one and is now composed.

5.criterion: Domain models retain legitimate non-person state outside AuraPersonIdentity
5.evidence: Holds everywhere converged; the directory keeps its selection key, subtitle and de-duplication invariant beside the person, not inside it.

6.criterion: All remaining measured hits classified and non-competing
6.evidence: The 19 previously measured hits are all classified and non-competing. The 29+8 now measured are classified, but 18 of them ARE competing.

f116FinalState.change: NO PROMOTION. The state reported at commit 57d1680 is withdrawn.

f053FinalState.structuralTest: Can one Aura person still acquire a different name, handle, avatar, fallback or address because different code interprets them differently? YES — and this pass found a live instance: the member directory addressed a person at '/$handle' while the canonical model addresses them at '/u/:handle', and only the second is a declared route. It also found an avatar alias list that accepted `avatar` where the canonical reader accepts `photoUrl`, and an invented 'Member' label. Those are fixed. `CorrespondenceIdentity` still carries its own orders.
f053FinalState.whatImproved: Typed boundaries are converged; the four protected Meetings models and both feed actors hold; the app shell, the member directory, the profile editor and two viewer-identity reads now resolve through the one reader.

meetingEntryResolutionSpecialCase.test: Person parsing canonical? YES — the MEMBER branch delegates to AuraPersonIdentity. Prefill chooses blank rather than inventing identity? YES — `identityName` returns null when nothing was resolved, and the test 'an unresolved entrant is still UNRESOLVED' pins that 'Someone' is never produced. Private alias or fallback chain remaining? NO.
meetingEntryResolutionSpecialCase.verdict: NOT counted as competing person semantics. Presentation declining the canonical label is a destination decision; the identity parsing behind it is canonical.

F052.effect: NO state change from this reconciliation, as instructed.

F054.effect: The Guest correction stands as implementation evidence and is NOT promoted. This pass adds a second instance of the same class — the directory's invented 'Member' label — now removed. Evidence accumulates; the finding's own contract was not re-audited.

F057.effect: Its defect class was directly re-encountered: the app-shell reader's own docstring described an F057-shaped bug it had been written to patch, and the profile editor's avatar list could resolve an avatar the rest of the product would not. Both converged. No state change claimed.

F051.effect: PRESERVED CONFLICT, UNTOUCHED. No chat avatar redesign, no universal avatar treatment, no conversation-avatar adjudication. Confirmed still CONFLICTING_CURRENT_STATE by validate-stage0.mjs.

measurementVsFindingState: They are not the same quantity and should not be forced to match. Surface debt now counts three different things: 15 AVATAR-class sites that render an already-canonical person without going through AuraAvatar (a presentation concern), 2 backend credential selects (a governed exception), and 12 USER_SHAPE map reads of which 10 are real person debt and 2 are institution reads the classifier's naming signals cannot resolve. A single number over three concerns is a risk indicator, not a finding state — which is precisely why the finding state is adjudicated here from provenance rather than read off the counter.
